23479.sol: The electrical nature of a material depends on the energy gap between the valence band and the conduction band. 123870.sol: The movement of chromosomes towards opposite poles indicates that the cell is in the anaphase stage of division. The key observation is that each chromosome consists of two chromatids joined at an undivided centromere. This means the centromere has not split. In anaphase of mitosis and anaphase II of meiosis, the centromeres split and sister chromatids separate to move to opposite poles. However, in Anaphase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres

124086.subject: Botany
124086.text: Based on the diagram, which type of chromosome has the centromere very close to one end, resulting in one very long arm and one very short arm?

124250.subject: Botany
124250.text: A common characteristic feature of plant sieve tube cells and most of mammalian erythrocytes is
124250.sol: A common characteristic feature of plant sieve tube cells and most of mammalian erythrocytes is absence of nucleus.

124296.subject: Botany
124296.text: A cell biologist extracts the dense homogeneous substance from the inner compartment of an isolated mitochondrion. Which of the following components will be absent in this extract?
124296.sol: The inner compartment of the mitochondrion is filled with a dense homogeneous substance called the matrix. According to NCERT, the mitochondrial matrix possesses a single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, and 70S ribosomes (along with the components required for the synthesis of proteins). It does not contain 80S ribosomes, which are characteristic of the eukaryotic cytoplasm and rough endoplasmic reticulum. Therefore, 80S ribosomes will be absent in the extract. Answer: 80S ribosomes

124548.subject: Botany
124548.text: What was identified as the active substance causing the Bakanae disease in rice seedlings?
124548.sol: The ‘bakane’ (foolish seedling) disease of rice seedlings, was caused by a fungal pathogen Gibberella fujikuroi. E. Kurosawa reported the appearance of symptoms of the disease in uninfected rice seedlings when they were treated with sterile filtrates of the fungus . The active substanceswere later identified as gibberellic acid.

124650.subject: Botany
124650.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Gibberellins cause fruits to elongate and improve its shape Reason: Gibberellins can promote early senescence
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
124650.sol: Gibberellins have the ability to cause an increase in length of axis is used to increase the length of grapes stalks. Gibberellins, cause fruits like apple to elongate and improve its shape. They also delay senescence.

124855.subject: Botany
124855.text: Identify (i), (ii) and (iii) in the given diagram.

125280.subject: Botany
125280.sol: Schizogony is stage in asexual reproduction of Plasmodium (malarial parasite) in which schizont is formed. From the human blood sporozoites enter the liver cells. The sporozoite grows in size to become a rounded schizont called cryptozoite. The latter divides to form cryptomerozoites ( = merozoites). The merozoites are asexual haploid forms. The host liver cells rupture to liberate the cryptomerozoites into the liver sinusoids.

125574.subject: Botany
125574.text: Experiment Observation A. Joseph Priestley 1) Plants restore air quality. B. Jan Ingenhousz 2) Sunlight is essential for purifying air. C. Candle in a closed jar 3) Air becomes "damaged." D. Mouse in a closed jar 4) Suffocates due to lack of air.
125574.sol: A - 4: Joseph Priestley concluded that plants restore the air quality. B - 2: Jan Ingenhousz demonstrated that sunlight is essential for plants to purify the air. C - 3: A burning candle in a closed jar "damages" the air, causing it to extinguish. D - 1: A mouse in a closed jar suffocates due to a lack of breathable air.

125651.subject: Botany
125651.text: A plant species shows initial CO ₂ fixation in cells that possess PEPcase but completely lack the RuBisCO enzyme. Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding this plant?
options: Its primary CO ₂ acceptor is a 5-carbon compound.
It possesses Kranz anatomy in its leaves.
It can tolerate higher temperatures compared to C ₃ plants.
It shows a negligible rate of photorespiration.
125651.sol: The plant described performs initial CO ₂ fixation in cells possessing PEPcase but lacking RuBisCO. This is a defining characteristic of the mesophyll cells of C ₄ plants. C ₄ plants exhibit special leaf anatomy called Kranz anatomy, tolerate higher temperatures, and show a negligible rate of photorespiration due to their internal CO ₂ concentrating mechanism. In C ₄ plants, the primary CO ₂ acceptor is phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), which is a 3-carbon compound. A 5-carbon compound (RuBP) acts as the primary acceptor

125662.subject: Botany
125662.text: Read the following statements carefully: (A) The splitting of water is associated with the PS II. (B) Stroma lamellae evolve oxygen during photosynthesis. (C) Cyclic photophosphorylation does not involve photolysis of water. (D) Grana lamellae membranes lack NADP reductase enzyme. How many of the above statements are correct?
125662.sol: Statement (A) is correct as the water splitting complex is associated with the PS II, which itself is physically located on the inner side of the membrane of the thylakoid. Statement (B) is incorrect because stroma lamellae lack PS II, and therefore cannot perform photolysis of water or evolve oxygen. Statement (C) is correct because cyclic photophosphorylation involves only PS I, whereas photolysis of water is strictly associated with PS II. Statement (D) is incorrect because grana lamellae membranes possess both

126027.subject: Botany
126027.text: Select the correct statement for the given figure.
options: Mature seeds may be Non-albuminous seeds that have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during e
As the seed matures, its water content is reduced and seeds become relatively dry (4-5 percent moisture by mas
Although in most of the species, fruits are the results of fertilisation, there are a few species in which fru
By the time the fruit develops from the ovary, other floral parts degenerate and fall off in all plants.
126027.sol: Mature seeds may be non-albuminous or ex-albuminous. Non- albuminous seeds have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during embryo development (e.g., pea, groundnut). Albuminous seeds retain a part of the endosperm as it is not completely used up during embryo development (e.g., wheat, maize, barley, castor). As the seed matures, its water content is reduced and seeds become relatively dry (10-15 per cent moisture by mass). In most plants, by the time the fruit develops from the ovary, other floral pa

126403.subject: Botany
126403.text: In ginger, vegetative propagation occurs through:
126403.sol: Rhizome: It is a thick stem growing horizontally, beneath the soil surface. It has distinct nodes and internodes. The nodes bear small scale leaves with buds in their axils. These buds develop into aerial shoot during favourable conditions. The tip of the rhizome ends in a terminal bud. The lower surfaces of the nodes give out small slender adventitious roots. E.g. ginger, turmeric, etc.

126438.subject: Botany
126438.text: Which of the following is the most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere?
126438.sol: Proteins carry out many functions in living organisms, some transport nutrients across cell membrane, some fight infectious organisms, some are hormones, some are enzymes.,Collagen is the most abundant protein in animal world and Ribulose bisphosphate Carboxylase-Oxygenase (RuBisCO) is the most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere .

126768.subject: Botany
126768.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : The inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate is a classic example of competitive inhibition. Reason (R) : Malonate closely resembles the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase in its molecular structure and competes with the product for the active site. In the light of the above statements, choose
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
126768.sol: Assertion (A) is a correct statement as per NCERT; the inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate is indeed a well-known example of competitive inhibition. Reason (R) is incorrect because a competitive inhibitor closely resembles the substrate (which is succinate in this case) in its molecular structure, not the enzyme itself. Furthermore, the inhibitor competes with the substrate for the active site of the enzyme, not with the product. Therefore, (A) is correct but (R) is not correct. Answer: (A) is correct

126830.subject: Botany
126830.text: Prosthetic groups differ from coenzymes in that
options: they require metal ions for their activity
they (prosthetic groups) are tightly bound to apoenzymes
their association with apoenzymes is transient
they can serve as cofactors in a number of enzyme catalysed reactions
126830.sol: Prosthetic groups are organic compounds and are distinguished from other cofactors in that they are tightly bound to the apoenzyme. For example, in peroxidase and catalase, which catalyse the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen, haem is the prosthetic group and it is a part of the active site of the enzyme.

126997.subject: Botany
126997.text: Climate of the world is threatened by:
options: increasing amount of atmospheric carbon dioxide.
decreasing amount of atmospheric carbon dioxide.
126997.sol: Carbon dioxide is the major greenhouse gas. It is capable of absorbing infrared radiation, trapping and holding heat in the atmosphere. By increasing the heat in the atmosphere, greenhouse gases are responsible for the greenhouse effect, which ultimately leads to global warming. Greenhouse gases include carbon dioxide, water vapour, methane, ozone, nitrous oxide and fluorinated gases they absorb heat and trap heat within the surface-troposphere system. Related Theory The various consequences of Global warming are:

127536.subject: Botany
127536.text: Newly formed Biosphere Reserve of India (2013) is
127536.sol: Panna Biosphere Reserve is situated in Chhattarpur Districts of Madhya Pradesh in India.

127985.subject: Zoology
127985.text: What type of sensory organs are absent in frogs?
127985.sol: Frog has different types of sense organs, namely organs of touch (sensory papillae), taste (taste buds), smell (nasal epithelium), vision (eyes) and hearing (tympanum with internal ears). Out of these, eyes and internal ears are well-organised structures and the rest are cellular aggregations around nerve endings. Eyes in a frog are a pair of spherical structures situated in the orbit in skull. These are simple eyes (possessing only one unit). External ear is absent in frogs and only tympanum can be seen externally

128165.subject: Zoology
128165.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding the reproductive structures of cockroaches. List-I List-II A. Spermatheca I. 6^ th to 7^ th abdominal segments in male B. Mushroom gland II. 9^ th sternum in male C. Anal style III. 6^ th abdominal segment in female D. Collaterial gland IV. Secretes hard egg case (ootheca) Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
128165.sol: Spermatheca is a part of the female reproductive system, present in the 6^ th abdominal segment. Mushroom gland is an accessory reproductive gland present in the 6^ th to 7^ th abdominal segments of male cockroaches. Anal styles are a pair of short, thread-like structures present only in males, projecting from the 9^ th sternum. Collaterial glands are present in female cockroaches and their secretion forms the hard egg case called ootheca. Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV. Answer: A-III, B-

128178.subject: Zoology
128178.text: In frogs, a special venous connection carries blood from the lower parts of the body to the kidneys before it returns to the heart. This specific venous connection is known as the:
128178.sol: In frogs, there are special venous connections present in the circulatory system. The venous connection that carries blood from the lower parts of the body to the kidneys is called the renal portal system. The hepatic portal system connects the liver and the intestine. The pulmocutaneous vein and hepatic vein are other blood vessels but do not form the portal system between the lower body and kidneys. Answer: Renal portal system

128265.subject: Zoology
128265.text: How do hormones act as intracellular messengers?
options: By releasing into the blood and being transported to a distantly located target organ
By being secreted by the organised endocrine glands
128265.sol: Endocrine glands lack ducts and are hence, called ductless glands. Their secretions are called hormones. The classical definition of hormone as a chemical produced by endocrine glands and released into the blood and transported to a distantly located target organ has current scientific definition as follows: Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts. The new definition covers a number of new molecules in addition to the hormones secreted by the organ

128716.subject: Zoology
128716.text: Which of the following teeth are lophodont?
128716.sol: The premolars and molars are called cheek teeth. These are also called lophodont teeth. Their free ends are flattened and bear transverse ridges to crush and grind the food.

128845.subject: Zoology
128845.text: What type of heart do fishes have?
128845.sol: All vertebrates possess a muscular chambered heart . Fishes have a 2-chambered heart with an atrium and a ventricle . Amphibians and the reptiles (except crocodiles) have a 3-chambered heart with two atria and a single ventricle, whereas crocodiles, birds and mammals possess a 4-chambered heart with two atria and two ventricles. In fishes the heart pumps out deoxygenated blood which is oxygenated by the gills and supplied to the body parts from where deoxygenated blood is returned to the heart (single circulation).

129245.subject: Zoology
129245.text: What is the inner part of the cerebral hemisphere called?
129245.sol: A deep cleft divides the cerebrum longitudinally into two halves, which are called the left and right cerebral hemispheres. The cerebral cortex contains motor areas, sensory areas, and large regions that are neither clearly sensory nor motor in function. These regions, called the association areas, are responsible for complex functions such as intersensory associations, memory and communication.The cerebral cortex contains motor areas, sensory areas, and large regions that are neither clearly sensory nor motor in f

129533.subject: Zoology
129533.text: What is the function of Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT) in urine formation?
options: Maintenance of osmolarity of medullary interstitial fluid
Conditional excretion of Na⁺ and water
Maintenance of pH and sodium-potassium balance in blood
129533.sol: Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT): Conditional reabsorption of Na+ and water takes place in this segment. DCT is also capable of reabsorption of HCO3– and selective secretion of hydrogen and potassium ions and NH3 to maintain the pH and sodium-potassium balance in blood. Collecting Duct: This long duct extends from the cortex of the kidney to the inner parts of the medulla. Large amounts of water could be reabsorbed from this region to produce a concentrated urine. This segment allows passage of small amounts of urea

129857.subject: Zoology
129857.sol: Alveoli are the primary sites of exchange of gases. Exchange of gases also occur between blood and tissues. O2 and CO2 are exchanged in these sites by simple diffusion mainly based on pressure/concentration gradient. Solubility of the gases as well as the thickness of the membranes involved in diffusion are also some important factors that can affect the rate of diffusion. Pressure contributed by an individual gas in a mixture of gases is called partial pressure and is represented as pO2 for oxygen and pCO2 for car

129864.subject: Zoology
129864.text: How much of CO₂ is transported by RBCs in the blood?
129864.sol: . Blood is the medium of transport for O2 and CO2. About 97 per cent of O2 is transported by RBCs in the blood. The remaining 3 per cent of O2 is carried in a dissolved state through the plasma. Nearly 20-25 per cent of CO2 is transported by RBCs whereas 70 per cent of it is carried as bicarbonate . About 7 per cent of CO2 is carried in a dissolved state through plasma. Chapter Name Breathing and Exchange of Gases Page Number:189 Paragraph Number:1 Topic:Transport of gases Concept:Introduction Difficulty Level:Medi

129927.subject: Zoology
129927.text: What is the role of the respiratory rhythm centre in regulating the respiratory system?
options: It regulates the oxygen levels in the blood
It controls the rate of breathing
It controls the depth of breathing
It controls the pattern of breathing
129927.sol: Human beings have a significant ability to maintain and moderate the respiratory rhythm to suit the demands of the body tissues. This is done by the neural system . A specialised centre present in the medulla region of the brain called respiratory rhythm centre is primarily responsible for this regulation . Another centre present in the pons region of the brain called pneumotaxic centre can moderate the functions of the respiratory rhythm centre. Neural signal from this centre can reduce the duration of inspiration

130012.subject: Zoology
130012.text: Component Function A. Nasal Cavity 1. Conducts air into the lungs B. Pharynx 2. Passage for air and food C. Epiglottis 3. Prevents food from entering the windpipe D. Bronchi 4. Moistens and filters air
130012.sol: The nasal cavity moistens and filters incoming air. The pharynx serves as a passage for both air and food. The epiglottis prevents food from entering the windpipe. The bronchi conduct air into the lungs.

130269.subject: Zoology
130269.text: What are the bones of the pelvic girdle?
130269.sol: The pectoral and pelvic girdle bones help in the articulation of the upper and the lower limbs respectively with the axial skeleton.Each half of the pectoral girdle consists of a clavicle and a scapula.The acromion is a slightly elevated ridge in the scapula that projects as a flat, expanded process and articulates with the clavicle. The pelvic girdle consists of two coxal bones. .The human body consists of 206 bones in total. These bones are grouped into two main divisions - the axial skeleton and the appendicular

130708.subject: Zoology
130708.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. Lactational amenorrhea is effective only upto a maximum period of five months 2. Chances of failure of natural methods of contraception is nil 3. Natural methods can prevent STIs 4. Lactational amenorrhea (absence of menstruation) method is based on the fact that ovulation and therefore the cycle do not occur during the period of intense lactation foll
130708.sol: As long as the mother breast-feeds the child fully, chances of conception are almost nil. However, this method has been reported to be effective only upto a maximum period of six months following parturition.

130733.subject: Zoology
130733.text: ___ for sex determination is banned in our country.
130733.sol: Amniocentesis for sex determination is banned in our country.

131877.subject: Zoology
131877.text: In prokaryotes, the core RNA polymerase enzyme on its own is capable of catalysing which specific step of transcription?
131877.sol: In prokaryotes, the RNA polymerase core enzyme is only capable of catalysing the process of elongation. It must associate transiently with the initiation factor ( ) to initiate transcription and with the termination factor ( ) to terminate the process. Therefore, without these transient factors, the core enzyme can only perform elongation. Answer: Elongation only

132163.subject: Zoology
132163.text: In the F2 generation, what proportion of plants had green seeds?
132163.sol: The genotype of the parents can then be written as RRYY and rryy. The cross between the two plants can be written down as in Figure 4.7 showing the genotypes of the parent plants. The gametes RY and ry unite on fertilisation to produce the F1 hybrid RrYy. When Mendel self hybridized the F1 plants he found that 3/4th of F2 plants had yellow seeds and 1/4th had green . The yellow and green color is segregated in a 3:1 ratio. Round and wrinkled seed shape is also segregated in a 3:1 ratio; just like in a monohybrid cr

132325.subject: Zoology
132325.text: Select the correct statement for the given figure.
options: The sex determination in honey bees is based on the number of sets of chromosomes the individual's parents rec
An offspring formed from the union of a sperm and an egg develops as a male, and an unfertilised egg develops
This is called a haplodiploid sex-determination system and has special characteristic features such as the mal
The males do not have fathers and thus cannot have sons, but have a grandfather and can have grandsons.
132325.sol: The sex determination in honey bees is based on the number of sets of chromosomes an individual receives. An offspring formed from the union of a sperm and an egg develops as a female (queen or worker), and an unfertilised egg develops as a male (drone) by means of parthenogenesis. This means that the males have half the number of chromosomes than that of a female. The females are diploid having 32 chromosomes and males are haploid, i.e., having 16 chromosomes. This is called a haplodiploid sex-determination system

132715.subject: Zoology
132715.text: What observation is natural selection based on according to the paragraph?
options: Members of a population vary in characteristics
All members of a population are identical
132715.sol: Natural selection is based on certain observations which are factual . For example, natural resources are limited, populations are stable in size except for seasonal fluctuation, members of a population vary in characteristics (infact no two individuals are alike) even though they look superficially similar, most of variations are inherited etc. The fact that theoretically population size will grow exponentially if everybody reproduced maximally (this fact can be seen in a growing bacterial population) and the fact

133790.subject: Zoology
133790.text: What is the key belief of the organic farmer?
options: The use of chemicals is necessary to control pests
The use of chemicals is harmful to the environment
A complex system of checks and balances is not necessary in a living and vibrant ecosystem
133790.sol: In agriculture, there is a method of controlling pests that relies on natural predation rather than introduced chemicals. A key belief of the organic farmer is that biodiversity furthers health . The more variety a landscape has, the more sustainable it is. The organic farmer, therefore, works to create a system where the insects that are sometimes called pests are not eradicated, but instead are kept at manageable levels by a complex system of checks and balances within a living and vibrant ecosystem

133962.subject: Zoology
133962.text: An agricultural scientist recommends organism X to control butterfly caterpillars, organism Y to treat root-borne plant pathogens, and organism Z to enhance phosphorus uptake in phosphorus-deficient soils. Identify X, Y, and Z from the given options.
options: X - Bacillus thuringiensis, Y - Trichoderma, Z - Glomus
X - Bacillus thuringiensis, Y - Glomus, Z - Trichoderma
X - Baculoviruses, Y - Trichoderma, Z - Rhizobium
X - Bacillus thuringiensis, Y - Trichoderma, Z - Rhizobium
133962.sol: Bacillus thuringiensis is a microbial biocontrol agent used specifically to control butterfly caterpillars. Trichoderma species are free-living fungi common in root ecosystems that act as effective biocontrol agents against several plant pathogens. Glomus is a genus of fungi that forms symbiotic mycorrhizal associations with plants, specifically helping in the absorption of phosphorus from the soil. Rhizobium fixes nitrogen rather than absorbing phosphorus, and Baculoviruses are insect pathogens but Bacillus thurin

134044.subject: Zoology
134044.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
134044.sol: Genetic variation present among plants cells of a culture is called somaclonal variation. The term is also used for the genetic variation present in plants regenerated from a single culture. This variation has been used to develop sexual/useful variations.

134092.subject: Zoology
134092.text: What type of crop plants are usually incorporated with Bt toxin genes?
134092.sol: Specific Bt toxin genes were isolated from Bacillus thuringiensis and incorporated into the several crop plants such as cotton The choice of genes depends upon the crop and the targeted pest, as most Bt toxins are insect-group specific . The toxin is coded by a gene cryIAc named cry. There are a number of them, for example, the proteins encoded by the genes cryIAc and cryIIAb control the cotton bollworms, that of cryIAb controls corn borer.

134440.subject: Zoology
134440.text: How many restriction enzymes are known today besides Hind II?
options: More than 900 restriction enzymes from over 2030 strains of bacteria
134440.sol: The first restriction endonuclease–Hind II, whose functioning depended on a specific DNA nucleotide sequence was isolated and characterized five years later. It was found that Hind II always cut DNA molecules at a particular point by recognizing a specific sequence of six base pairs. This specific base sequence is known as the recognition sequence for Hind II. Besides Hind II, today we know more than 900 restriction enzymes that have been isolated from over 230 strains of bacteria each of which recognize different

135011.subject: Zoology
135011.text: Assertion : Restriction enzymes cut the strand of DNA to produce sticky ends. Reason: Stickiness of the ends facilitates the action of the enzyme DNA polymerase.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
135011.sol: Restriction enzyme, a type of endonuclease, functions by "inspecting" the length of a DNA sequence. Once it finds a recognition sequence, it binds and cut each of the two strands of the double helix at specific point leaving single stranded portions at the ends. This results in overhanging stretches called sticky ends. These in the same individual. These are called bisexual or monoecious animals or hermaphrodites. In these animals, testes and ovaries do not mature simultaneously. For example in earthworm, testes ma

135052.subject: Zoology
135052.text: What does the age pyramid for a human population typically show?
options: Age distribution of males and females
135052.sol: Another attribute characteristic of a population is sex ratio. An individual is either a male or a female but a population has a sex ratio (e.g., 60 percent of the population are females and 40 per cent males). A population at any given time is composed of individuals of different ages. If the age distribution (percent individuals of a given age or age group) is plotted for the population, the resulting structure is called an age pyramid (Figure 11.1). For the human population , the age pyramids generally show the

135134.subject: Zoology
135134.text: What did Darwin believe to be a potent force in organic evolution?
135134.sol: When Darwin spoke of the struggle for existence and survival of the fittest in nature, he was convinced that interspecific competition is a potent force in organic evolution . It is generally believed that competition occurs when closely related species compete for the same resources that are limiting, but this is not entirely true. Firstly, totally unrelated species could also compete for the same resource. For instance, in some shallow South American lakes, visiting flamingoes and resident fishes compete for thei

135416.subject: Zoology
135416.text: A population ecologist recorded the initial population size and the number of new births over a period of one month for four different insect species in a laboratory. The data is presented below: Species P: Initial population = 50 , New births = 15 Species Q: Initial population = 200 , New births = 40 Species R: Initial population = 10 , New births = 4 Species S: Initial population = 100 , New births = 25 Which speci
135416.sol: The per capita birth rate is calculated by dividing the number of new births by the initial population size. For Species P: 15 50 = 0.30 For Species Q: 40 200 = 0.20 For Species R: 4 10 = 0.40 For Species S: 25 100 = 0.25 Comparing the values, Species R has the highest per capita birth rate ( 0.40 ). Students may incorrectly choose Species Q if they only look at the highest absolute number of births ( 40 ) without calculating the per capita rate. Answer: Species R

6a104ffb8b46719ce7976d1f.subject: Chemistry
6a104ffb8b46719ce7976d1f.text: Identify the major products A and B formed in the following reaction sequence.

The - OH group is directly replaced by a - Cl atom. Product A is CH ₃- CH ₂- CH(Cl) - CH(CH ₃)₂ , which is named 3-chloro-2-methylpentane. Reaction with alc. KOH , Alcoholic KOH with heat brings about dehydrohalogenation

options: Air flows from the smaller bubble to the larger bubble.
Air flows from the larger bubble to the smaller bubble.
Air does not flow as the system is already in pressure equilibrium.
Air flows from the larger to the smaller bubble until their sizes become equal.

Answer: Air flows from the smaller bu

6a2109af219e1ae5a1722939.subject: Physics
6a2109af219e1ae5a1722939.text: A steady current I enters a circuit at node P and leaves at node Q . The circuit consists of two parallel branches between P and Q . The upper branch contains a single resistor of resistance R₁ . The lower branch contains two resistors in series, having resistances R₂ and R₃ . If I₂ is the current flowing through R₂ , what is the ratio I₂ I ?
6a2109af219e1ae5a1722939.sol: The circuit consists of two parallel branches between nodes P and Q . The resistance of the upper branch is R_ upper = R₁ . The resistance of the lower branch is R_ lower = R₂ + R₃ , as the two resistors are in series. Since the branches are in parallel, the potential difference V across both branches is the same. The current through the lower branch is I₂ = V R₂ + R₃ . The total current I is given by I = V R_ eq , where R_ eq is the equivalent resistance of the circuit. 1 R_ eq = 1 R₁ + 1 R₂ + R₃ = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ R₁

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
6a104ffd8b46719ce7976d5a.sol: Statement I is false because in cortical nephrons, the loop of Henle is short and extends only very little into the medulla. It is the juxtamedullary nephrons that have a very long loop of Henle running deep into the medulla. 96155.subject: Botany
96155.text: In an organism, if the normal diploid number of chromosomes is 8, how many chromatids are present in each daughter cell at the end of meiosis I
96155.sol: Meiosis I ends when the chromosomes of each homologous pair arrive at opposing poles of the cell. The microtubules disintegrate, and a new nuclear membrane forms around each haploid set of chromosomes. The chromosomes uncoil, forming chromatin again, and cytokinesis occurs, forming two non-identical daughter cells. A resting phase known as interkinesis or interphase II happens in some organisms. Therefore, each daughter cell will have 4 chromosomes and 8 chromatids, at the end of the meiosis I.

96535.text: Which of the following correctly represent the pyramid of biomass in aquatic ecosystem?
96535.sol: The total biomass of each trophic level can be represented by using a pyramid of biomass. In most ecosystems, the pyramid of biomass is an upright one. But in the aquatic ecosystem, the biomass pyramid is inverted. This is because the primary producers in the aquatic ecosystem are the phytoplanktons. These phytoplanktons are micro organisms and thus have very little biomass as compared to the aquatic animals who consume them and occupy the successive trophic levels in the food chain.

96589.subject: Botany
96589.text: Select the WRONG statement regarding energy flow in an ecosystem.
options: Energy flow in one direction only
About 1-5% of the energy reaching the ground is converted by the green plants into chemical energy.
Energy requirement for maintenance of body gradually decreases in successive trophic levels.
Only 10% of the gross productivity of producers is entrapped by herbivores for their body building.
96589.sol: A community of organisms interacting with abiotic component in a particular region/area will be called as ecosystem. The living and non-living components are linked together by the nutrient cycles and energy flow through each trophic level. In a typical food chain, the energy that is transferred from one trophic level to the next is always unidirectional and never forms a cyclical pattern. The main source of energy is the sun (solar energy/free energy), which is used by producers to make food and then it is consume

97322.sol: Growth rate is measured by increased growth per unit time. Growth in an organism or its part can occur in many different ways. When the total growth of the living system is measured and compared in a particular unit time is referred as absolute growth rate. This growth rate is for that particular living system in that time interval and not compared with other living system. Absolute growth = Growth in given time period = Growth (final time) - Growth (initial time) Absolute growth of A = Growth A'-Growth A = 10 - 5

306685.subject: Physics
306685.text: The statement that heat and work are equivalent implies that
options: a body initially at rest can be set into linear motion by providing heat to it
when heat is provided to a body, we perform work on it
when work is performed on a body, we provide heat to it
the temperature of a body can be raised by performing work on it
306685.sol: The equivalence of heat and work implies that both are forms of energy transfer that can produce the same effect on a system. According to Joule's principle of the mechanical equivalent of heat, mechanical work done on a system can increase its internal energy, which manifests as a rise in its temperature. This produces the exact same effect as supplying heat to the system. Therefore, the temperature of a body can be raised by performing work on it.
